question: What Are Pressure Sensing Lines?
body_html:
Pressure sensing lines, also called impulse lines, are small pipes or tubes that connect the process pressure tapping point to the pressure transmitter, so it can be mounted away from heat, vibration and corrosion.

Liquid lines should slope downward toward the process and gas lines upward, typically 10 cm per metre.

The main causes of measurement error are voids (trapped air or gas), blockages, leakage and freezing when heat tracing fails. Trapped air on the low side of a DP transmitter reads higher than actual DP.
